Sydney Sweeney’s latest ad has reignited the familiar argument over whether women are being empowered or objectified—but Russell wonders whether the argument itself is the trap. As the culture invites us to obsess over Sweeney’s body or condemn others for doing exactly that, he attempts the considerably harder task of not looking at her at all, while asking whether either side of the culture war brings us any closer to something meaningful.

author: Russell Brand
description:
A deeply personal exchange with one of Russell’s fans turns into a conversation about what it actually feels like to experience the presence of God.

The fan describes getting goosebumps and feeling the hairs on his arms stand up while praying, asking whether that physical sensation could be the Holy Spirit. Russell reflects on similar experiences and suggests that rather than dismissing those moments as random bodily reactions, perhaps we should pay closer attention to them.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell’s guest argues that Covid and the lockdowns amounted to the largest exercise in mass control of human beings in history — even greater in scale than a World War — and describes the vaccine rollout as the biggest injection of a consumer product ever, far beyond something like Coca-Cola in terms of reach, often with people not fully understanding what they were taking part in.

They push the thought experiment further, asking: what if it was already known that the mRNA would not remain in the arm, that it could cross the blood-brain barrier and reach organs such as the ovaries, potentially causing harm — and that this was understood beforehand rather than discovered later?

The conversation then turns to the idea of being gaslit into doubting your own perception of reality. Yet they find one unexpected silver lining in that distortion: more people than ever may now be seriously questioning what is real, what they are told, and who they trust.
